units.title: Unit 1: Inside the World of Care

questions.prompt: Nurse Sarah works from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m. this week, so she is on the night ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ shift = a fixed period of working time, especially in hospitals and factories (وردية / نوبة عمل). We say "on the night shift" or "on the day shift".
✗ round: a doctor's or nurse's regular visits to the patients in a ward (a ward round), not the whole working period.
✗ term: a part of the school or university year — not a period of hospital work.
✗ season: a part of the year (summer, winter) or of a sports competition.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "shift" have the same meaning as in "Sarah's 12-hour shift starts at seven"?
options: Press the Shift key to type a capital letter.
Factory workers get extra pay for the night shift.
There has been a big shift in people's opinions.
Can you help me shift this heavy bed?
questions.answer: Factory workers get extra pay for the night shift.
questions.explanation:
✓ "Factory workers get extra pay for the night shift." — as in the story, shift = a set period of working time (وردية).
✗ "the Shift key": the name of a key on a computer keyboard.
✗ "a big shift in people's opinions": here shift = a change.
✗ "shift this heavy bed": here shift is a verb = move something to another place.

questions.prompt: "The man groaned as the paramedics lifted him onto the stretcher." Which word is the closest in meaning to "groaned"?
questions.explanation:
✓ moaned: to groan (يئن) and to moan (يتأوه) both mean to make a long, low sound because of pain — he was hurt, so being lifted made him groan.
✗ grinned: smiled widely — not what an injured man does while being lifted.
✗ beeped: made a short electronic sound, like a machine.
✗ grabbed: took hold of something quickly — an action with the hands, not a sound.

questions.prompt: From early morning, the hospital is ___ with activity: doctors hurry along the corridors and patients wait to be seen.
questions.explanation:
✓ buzzing with activity = full of busy people and noise (مليء بالحركة والضجيج). A buzz is the sound of many people talking or machines working.
✗ collapsing: falling down suddenly — it does not go with "with activity".
✗ beeping: the short, high electronic sound a machine makes — machines beep, but a place is not "beeping with activity".
✗ moaning: making a long, low sound of pain or unhappiness — a person's sound; it does not describe a busy place.

questions.prompt: As the guests arrived at the wedding, a happy ___ of conversation filled the hall.
questions.explanation:
✓ buzz = the sound of many people talking together (همهمة / ضجيج أصوات). "A buzz of conversation" is a common phrase.
✗ groan: a deep sound that shows pain or unhappiness — it does not fit a happy wedding.
✗ beep: a short, high sound made by a machine, not by people talking.
✗ pulse: the beating of the heart, not a sound of conversation.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "buzz" mean "the sound of many people talking or machines working"?
options: She gets a real buzz from helping sick children.
I'll give you a buzz when I get home.
The boys were told to buzz off and stop shouting.
The busy factory was full of the buzz of machines.
questions.answer: The busy factory was full of the buzz of machines.
questions.explanation:
✓ "the buzz of machines" = the continuous sound of machines working (طنين / ضجيج الآلات) — the meaning taught in the unit.
✗ "gets a real buzz from": gets a strong feeling of pleasure and excitement.
✗ "give you a buzz": an informal way of saying "phone you".
✗ "buzz off": a rude way of saying "go away".

questions.prompt: Every time a patient presses the call button, a machine at the nurses' desk ___ twice.
questions.explanation:
✓ beep = make a short, high electronic sound (يُصدر صفارة / صوت تنبيه). Machines, alarms and monitors beep.
✗ collapses: falls down suddenly — it is not a sound at all.
✗ groans: makes a deep sound of pain — a person's sound, not a machine's signal.
✗ moans: makes a long, low sound of pain or unhappiness — a person does this, not a machine giving a signal.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "In the emergency room, the monitors were ___, and the waiting area was ___ with voices."
questions.explanation:
✓ beeping – buzzing: monitors make short electronic sounds (beep), and a room full of people talking is "buzzing with voices" (ضجيج أصوات).
✗ buzzing – beeping: "the monitors were buzzing" is possible, but a waiting area cannot be "beeping with voices" — a beep is a machine's sound.
✗ groaning – beeping: groaning is a sound of pain made by people, not monitors, and voices do not beep.
✗ beeping – clutching: clutch means hold something tightly — it is not a sound.

questions.prompt: Only a qualified nurse is allowed to ___ this medication to patients.
questions.explanation:
✓ administer = give medicine or treatment to someone (يُعطي الدواء / العلاج): "administer medication to patients".
✗ admire: like and respect someone or something.
✗ admit: accept someone into a hospital (admit a patient to hospital), or agree that something is true.
✗ advise: tell someone what you think they should do — we advise a patient to take a medicine; we do not "advise medication to" patients.

questions.prompt: The ___ of the vaccine must be carried out by trained staff only.
questions.explanation:
✓ administration (noun) = the act of giving a medicine or treatment (إعطاء). After "The … of" we need a noun for an action.
✗ administrator: a noun, but it is a person who manages an office or organisation — a person cannot "be carried out".
✗ administrative: an adjective (connected with managing an organisation); an adjective cannot stand alone after "The" here.
✗ administer: the verb; a verb cannot follow "The".

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses "administer" correctly?
options: He administered that he had made a mistake.
The nurse administered the old man to the hospital.
The doctor administered a painkiller to the injured driver.
The teacher administered the students' beautiful drawings.
questions.answer: The doctor administered a painkiller to the injured driver.
questions.explanation:
✓ "administered a painkiller to the injured driver" = gave him the medicine (أعطاه الدواء) — the exact meaning in the unit.
✗ "administered that he had made a mistake": the right verb is admitted (agreed that it was true).
✗ "administered the old man to the hospital": the right verb is admitted (accepted him as a patient).
✗ "administered the students' beautiful drawings": the right verb is admired (looked at them with pleasure).

questions.prompt: The lifeguard ___ first aid to the boy he had pulled out of the sea until the paramedics arrived.
questions.explanation:
✓ administered first aid = gave first aid (قدّم الإسعافات الأولية). "Administer" is used with medicine, treatment and first aid.
✗ admitted: accepted someone into hospital, or agreed that something was true.
✗ assisted: we assist a person (assist the doctor), not "assist first aid to" someone.
✗ attended: we attend a course or a meeting (attend a first-aid course), but we do not "attend first aid to" someone.

questions.prompt: Mr. Ramy is still recovering from his operation, so he needs extra ___ from the nurses.
questions.explanation:
✓ attention = care given to someone (رعاية / اهتمام). A patient who is recovering needs extra attention.
✗ tension: a feeling of worry and stress.
✗ attendance: being present at a place, such as school or a meeting.
✗ intention: a plan, or something you want to do.

questions.prompt: The victims' injuries were serious and needed immediate medical ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ attention (noun): "immediate medical attention" = fast medical care (رعاية طبية فورية). This is a very common phrase.
✗ attendant: a person whose job is to help people (a flight attendant), not the care itself.
✗ attendance: being present somewhere — injuries do not need "attendance".
✗ attentive: an adjective (careful to listen and help); it cannot end the phrase after "medical".

questions.prompt: The doctor's calm, friendly words ___ the child's attention away from the pain of the injection.
questions.explanation:
✓ draw someone's attention away from something = make them stop noticing it and notice something else (صرف انتباهه). The doctor helped the child stop thinking about the pain.
✗ made: "make attention" is not an English phrase.
✗ paid: we "pay attention to" something — it describes the person who is listening, and it is not used with "away from".
✗ gave: we can "give something our attention", but "gave the child's attention away" is not correct English.

questions.prompt: Three passengers were badly hurt, and the accident ___ were rushed to the nearest hospital.
questions.explanation:
✓ victims = people who are hurt or killed by something bad, such as an accident or a crime (ضحايا). The hurt passengers are the victims.
✗ culprits: people who are guilty of doing something wrong.
✗ volunteers: people who offer to help without being paid.
✗ witnesses: people who see an accident or a crime happen; they are not the ones who were hurt.

questions.prompt: Many elderly people ___ victim to the flu virus last winter.
questions.explanation:
✓ fall victim to something = be hurt or harmed by it (وقع ضحية لـ). It is a fixed expression: fall – fell – fallen.
✗ went: "go victim to" is not English.
✗ got: "get victim to" is not English.
✗ made: "make victim to" is not English.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses "victim" correctly?
options: She was the victim of the race and won a gold medal.
The paramedics were the victims who saved his life.
The victim stole the old man's wallet.
Two victims of the fire are still in hospital.
questions.answer: Two victims of the fire are still in hospital.
questions.explanation:
✓ "Two victims of the fire are still in hospital." — victims are people who are hurt by something bad, such as a fire, an accident or a crime (ضحايا).
✗ "She was the victim of the race and won a gold medal": a person who wins is the winner, not a victim.
✗ "The paramedics were the victims who saved his life": the paramedics helped; they were not hurt — they were the rescuers.
✗ "The victim stole the old man's wallet": the person who steals is the thief (the culprit); the old man is the victim.

questions.prompt: Despite the ___ in the emergency room, Nurse Noura stayed calm and gave clear instructions.
questions.explanation:
✓ chaos = a state of complete confusion and disorder (فوضى). "Despite" shows a contrast: the room was in disorder, but she stayed calm.
✗ harmony: peaceful agreement — staying calm in harmony is not a contrast.
✗ order: everything organised — the opposite of chaos, so there is no contrast.
✗ silence: no noise — staying calm in silence is not surprising, so "Despite" makes no sense.

questions.prompt: After the bus crash, the emergency room was a ___ scene, with injured people and doctors everywhere.
questions.explanation:
✓ chaotic (adjective) = completely confused and disorganised (فوضوي). An adjective is needed before the noun "scene".
✗ chaos: the noun; we say "There was chaos", not "a chaos scene".
✗ calm: an adjective, but it is the opposite of what the sentence describes (injured people and doctors everywhere).
✗ chaotically: an adverb; it describes how something is done, not a noun.

questions.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "chaos"?
questions.explanation:
✓ order: a state in which everything is organised and in its correct place (نظام) — the opposite of chaos (فوضى).
✗ disorder: a synonym of chaos (a state with no order), not its opposite.
✗ panic: a sudden strong fear; it often happens in chaos, so it is not the opposite.
✗ confusion: a synonym of chaos, not its opposite.

questions.prompt: It was ___ to see the little boy crying for his lost mother in the busy hospital.
questions.explanation:
✓ heartbreaking = making you feel very sad (مُحزن جدًا). The -ing adjective describes the situation that causes the sadness: "It was heartbreaking to see…".
✗ heartbroken: describes the person who feels very sad (the boy was heartbroken), not the situation.
✗ heartbreakingly: an adverb (heartbreakingly sad); it cannot follow "It was" on its own.
✗ heartbreak: a noun (great sadness); "It was heartbreak to see" is not correct.

questions.prompt: When her grandmother died, Mona was ___ and could not stop crying.
questions.explanation:
✓ heartbroken = feeling extremely sad (حزين جدًا / مكسور القلب). It describes how a person feels.
✗ heartwarming: making you feel happy and pleased — the opposite feeling.
✗ heartbreaking: describes something that makes others sad; "Mona was heartbreaking" would mean she made other people sad.
✗ rewarding: giving satisfaction because you did something good — it does not fit sad news.

questions.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "heartbreaking"?
questions.explanation:
✓ joyful = very happy, or causing people to be happy (مُبهج / مُفرح) — the opposite of heartbreaking (مُحزن جدًا).
✗ tragic: very sad — a synonym, not an opposite.
✗ upsetting: making you unhappy or worried — close in meaning to heartbreaking.
✗ painful: causing pain or sadness — also close in meaning.

questions.prompt: Nursing is a tiring job, but it is very ___ because you help people every single day.
questions.explanation:
✓ rewarding = giving you a feeling of satisfaction because you help people or achieve something good (مُجزٍ / يمنح الرضا). "but" introduces the positive side of a tiring job.
✗ boring: not interesting — it is negative, so it does not contrast with "tiring".
✗ chaotic: full of disorder — again a negative idea that does not fit "because you help people".
✗ heartbreaking: very sad — it does not explain why helping people is good.

questions.prompt: Teachers often say that seeing their students succeed is the most ___ part of their job.
questions.explanation:
✓ rewarding = giving satisfaction (مُجزٍ). The -ing adjective describes the part of the job that gives this feeling.
✗ rewards: a plural noun (prizes or payments); it cannot come between "the most" and the noun "part".
✗ awarded: given officially as a prize ("She was awarded a medal").
✗ rewarded: describes a person who receives a reward ("He was rewarded for his hard work"), not a part of a job.

questions.prompt: "Some moments were heartbreaking, but many were rewarding." Here, "rewarding" means that these moments ___.
options: gave Sarah a feeling of satisfaction
questions.answer: gave Sarah a feeling of satisfaction
questions.explanation:
✓ gave Sarah a feeling of satisfaction: "rewarding" means giving pleasure and satisfaction because you helped someone or did something good (مُجزٍ معنويًا).
✗ earned Sarah extra money: a reward can be money, but "rewarding" here is about a good feeling, not payment.
✗ won Sarah a prize: that would be "she was awarded a prize".
✗ made Sarah feel very tired: that would be "tiring" or "exhausting".

questions.prompt: "Nursing is a never-ending rollercoaster." The writer means that nursing is ___.
options: a fun day out at a theme park
full of emotional ups and downs
a job that moves you from city to city
questions.answer: full of emotional ups and downs
questions.explanation:
✓ full of emotional ups and downs: a rollercoaster is a situation with many happy and sad moments one after the other (تقلبات مستمرة) — like the sad and rewarding moments of Sarah's day.
✗ dangerous because of fast machines: the word is used figuratively here, not about real machines.
✗ a fun day out at a theme park: this is the literal meaning (the ride), not what the writer means.
✗ a job that moves you from city to city: a rollercoaster has nothing to do with travelling for work.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses "rollercoaster" in the same way as "Nursing is a never-ending rollercoaster"?
options: The rollercoaster stopped, and the riders were stuck at the top.
This year has been a rollercoaster: I failed one exam, then came top in the next.
The children screamed on the rollercoaster at the theme park.
A new rollercoaster has opened near the beach.
questions.answer: This year has been a rollercoaster: I failed one exam, then came top in the next.
questions.explanation:
✓ "This year has been a rollercoaster…" — used figuratively: a time full of ups and downs (تقلبات), just as nursing has sad and rewarding moments.
✗ "The rollercoaster stopped… stuck at the top": the real ride — the literal meaning, not a situation with ups and downs.
✗ "screamed on the rollercoaster at the theme park": the real ride — the literal meaning.
✗ "A new rollercoaster has opened": the real ride — the literal meaning.

questions.prompt: "Nursing is full of ups and downs: some moments make Sarah very sad, and others give her great satisfaction." Which words describe nursing and these two kinds of moments?
questions.explanation:
✓ a rollercoaster – heartbreaking – rewarding: nursing has many ups and downs (a rollercoaster), the sad moments are heartbreaking (مُحزنة جدًا), and the satisfying ones are rewarding (مُجزية).
✗ joyful – tiring: joyful is the opposite of very sad, and tiring is not the same as giving satisfaction.
✗ heartbroken – rewarded: these describe a person (Sarah is heartbroken; she was rewarded), not the moments themselves.
✗ chaos: complete disorder — it does not mean ups and downs of feeling.

questions.prompt: The hospital's health awareness week will ___ on Sunday with free blood-pressure checks for everyone.
questions.explanation:
✓ kick off = start or begin (يبدأ / ينطلق). Events, matches and meetings kick off.
✗ kick up: as in "kick up a fuss" = complain loudly; it does not mean start.
✗ kick out: force someone to leave a place (kick him out of the club).
✗ kick back: relax.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "kick off" have the same meaning as in "Nurse Sarah kicks off her day with a cup of coffee"?
options: The final match kicks off at 9 p.m.
He kicked off his shoes and lay on the sofa.
The referee kicked the player off the pitch.
The painkiller will kick in after twenty minutes.
questions.answer: The final match kicks off at 9 p.m.
questions.explanation:
✓ "The final match kicks off at 9 p.m." — kick off = start (يبدأ), the same meaning as starting her day.
✗ "kicked off his shoes": took his shoes off quickly by shaking his feet — a literal meaning.
✗ "kicked the player off the pitch": made him leave — a different meaning.
✗ "kick in": a different phrasal verb; it means start to have an effect (for a medicine).

questions.prompt: "The meeting kicked off with a short talk about hospital safety." Which has the same meaning as "kicked off"?
questions.explanation:
✓ began: kick off = start (يبدأ / ينطلق).
✗ was put off: was postponed to a later time.
✗ broke up: ended, and the people left.
✗ was called off: was cancelled.

questions.prompt: Patients must not stop taking their ___ without asking their doctor first.
questions.explanation:
✓ medication = medicine or drugs given to treat an illness (دواء / أدوية).
✗ dedication: hard work and commitment to something.
✗ mediation: helping two sides who disagree to reach an agreement.
✗ meditation: sitting quietly and calming your mind — not something a doctor gives you to take.

questions.prompt: She has been taking a new ___ for her high blood pressure, and it has worked well.
questions.explanation:
✓ medication (noun) = a medicine you take to treat an illness (دواء).
✗ medicinal: an adjective (medicinal plants = plants used as medicine); it needs a noun after it.
✗ medic: a person, not a medicine — an informal word for a doctor or a medical student.
✗ medical: usually an adjective (medical care); as a noun, "a medical" is a health check — not something you take every day.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "Doctors usually ___ medicines, and nurses ___ them to the patients."
questions.explanation:
✓ prescribe – administer: the doctor prescribes (decides which medicine the patient needs and writes it down — يصف), and the nurse administers it (gives it — يُعطي).
✗ administer – prescribe: the jobs are the wrong way round; nurses usually do not decide which medicine a patient needs.
✗ prescribe – admit: "admit" means accept someone into hospital or agree that something is true; you do not "admit medicines to" patients.
✗ prescribe – stitch: you stitch a cut, not a medicine.

questions.prompt: "When the injured driver was rushed in, the team sprang into action." This means the team ___.
options: jumped up and down with joy
questions.explanation:
✓ spring into action = suddenly start working or responding quickly (بدأ العمل فورًا وبسرعة). It is an idiom, so "sprang" does not mean real jumping.
✗ jumped up and down with joy: this takes "spring" literally, and nobody is happy about an accident.
✗ refused to help the driver: the opposite of what the idiom means.
✗ took a short break: the opposite — they started working at once.

questions.prompt: Which expression has the SAME meaning as "spring into action"?
questions.explanation:
✓ jump into action = start doing something quickly and with energy (يبدأ العمل فورًا) — the same idea as spring into action.
✗ go the extra mile: make more effort than is expected of you.
✗ "Actions speak louder than words.": what you do matters more than what you say — it is not about starting quickly.
✗ out of action: not working or not able to work, for example because of an injury — almost the opposite.

questions.prompt: The moment the alarm sounded, the firefighters ___. Within seconds, they were in the fire engine.
questions.explanation:
✓ sprang into action = started working at once, quickly (بدأوا العمل فورًا). "The moment" and "within seconds" show speed.
✗ went the extra mile: doing more than is expected — the sentence is about how fast they started, not about extra effort.
✗ said "no pain, no gain": a saying about hard work and its results; it does not describe a fast reaction.
✗ were soaked to the skin: completely wet — nothing in the sentence is about rain or water.

questions.prompt: "Teamwork makes the dream work," Nurse Sarah often says. She means that ___.
options: you must work hard, even when it is painful, to succeed
people can achieve great things when they work together
you should do more than you are asked to do
one strong leader should make every decision
questions.answer: people can achieve great things when they work together
questions.explanation:
✓ people can achieve great things when they work together: the saying means that working as a team helps you reach your goals (بالعمل الجماعي تتحقق الأحلام). Sarah relies on her colleagues.
✗ you must work hard, even when it is painful, to succeed: this is the meaning of "No pain, no gain" — it says nothing about working together.
✗ you should do more than you are asked to do: this is "go the extra mile".
✗ one strong leader should make every decision: the opposite idea — the saying is about the whole team working together.

questions.prompt: Which saying is the closest in meaning to "Teamwork makes the dream work"?
questions.explanation:
✓ "Many hands make light work." — when many people help, a job becomes easy. Both sayings praise working together (العمل الجماعي).
✗ "Actions speak louder than words.": what you do matters more than what you say.
✗ "Better late than never.": it is better to do something late than not to do it at all.
✗ "No pain, no gain.": about working hard, even when it is difficult, to succeed — it says nothing about working with others.

questions.prompt: "Nurse Sarah always goes the extra mile for her patients." This means she ___.
options: only does what her job requires
does more than is expected of her
believes that hard work always brings success
questions.answer: does more than is expected of her
questions.explanation:
✓ go the extra mile = make more effort than is expected of you (يبذل جهدًا أكبر من المطلوب).
✗ starts working quickly, without hesitation: this is "spring / jump into action" — about speed, not extra effort.
✗ only does what her job requires: the opposite — going the extra mile means doing more than that.
✗ believes that hard work always brings success: this is closer to "No pain, no gain".

questions.prompt: The paramedic didn't just take the old man to hospital; she ___ and stayed with him until his family arrived.
questions.explanation:
✓ went the extra mile = did more than her job required (بذلت جهدًا أكبر من المطلوب). Taking him to hospital was her job; staying with him was extra. "didn't just …" shows this.
✗ jumped into action: starting to work quickly — the sentence is about doing more, not about speed.
✗ was soaked to the skin: completely wet — it has no link with staying with the patient.
✗ was pale as a ghost: very pale because of fear or illness — it does not explain why she stayed.

questions.prompt: Which situation is the best example of "No pain, no gain"?
options: Omar hurt his knee, so he stopped training and felt better.
Omar took a painkiller before the match.
Omar trained hard every day for months and finally joined the national team.
Omar won the match easily without any training.
questions.answer: Omar trained hard every day for months and finally joined the national team.
questions.explanation:
✓ Omar trained hard for months and then succeeded: "No pain, no gain" means you must work hard, even when it is difficult or painful, to achieve something (لا نجاح بدون تعب).
✗ He stopped training and felt better: there is no hard work and no achievement here.
✗ He took a painkiller: this takes "pain" literally; the saying is about effort, not medicine.
✗ He won without any training: this is gain without effort — the opposite of the saying.

questions.prompt: According to Unit 1, an idiom is ___.
options: a short story that teaches a moral lesson
a word that has the same meaning as another word
a fixed group of words whose meaning can't be guessed from the meanings of the separate words
a word made from the first letters of other words, such as CPR
questions.answer: a fixed group of words whose meaning can't be guessed from the meanings of the separate words
questions.explanation:
✓ An idiom (تعبير اصطلاحي) is a fixed expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of its single words — "raining cats and dogs" has nothing to do with animals.
✗ a short story that teaches a lesson: this is a fable, a story with a moral.
✗ a word with the same meaning as another word: this is a synonym.
✗ a word made from first letters, such as CPR: this is an acronym, a kind of abbreviation (CPR = cardiopulmonary resuscitation, said letter by letter) — not an idiom.

questions.prompt: Which of these would a nurse most likely describe as "rewarding"?
options: seeing a patient she cared for leave the hospital healthy
arriving at work soaked to the skin
filling in the same form again and again
watching a family hear very bad news
questions.answer: seeing a patient she cared for leave the hospital healthy
questions.explanation:
✓ seeing a patient she cared for leave healthy: this gives her satisfaction because she helped someone (مُجزٍ).
✗ arriving at work soaked to the skin: being completely wet from the rain is unpleasant, not rewarding.
✗ filling in the same form again and again: boring, repeated work — it does not give the feeling of having helped someone.
✗ watching a family hear very bad news: this is heartbreaking, not rewarding.

questions.prompt: After running up ten flights of stairs, the old man felt dizzy and suddenly ___ on the floor.
questions.explanation:
✓ collapsed = fell down suddenly, usually because of illness or weakness (انهار / سقط فجأة).
✗ elapsed: (of time) passed — "Two hours elapsed".
✗ collected: brought things together, or picked something up.
✗ collided: crashed into something or someone (two cars collided).

questions.prompt: The sudden ___ of the company left hundreds of workers without jobs.
questions.explanation:
✓ collapse (noun) = a sudden failure (انهيار). People and buildings collapse (fall down), and companies and plans collapse too (fail suddenly) — exams use both meanings.
✗ collection: a group of things gathered together (a stamp collection).
✗ collision: a crash in which two vehicles or people hit each other, or one hits something (a collision between two cars).
✗ consciousness: being awake and aware — a company cannot lose or have it.

questions.prompt: A building can collapse, a person can collapse, and a plan can collapse. In all three, "collapse" means ___.
options: become weaker slowly over many years
stop for a short time and then start again
be pushed over by someone else
questions.explanation:
✓ fall down or fail suddenly (ينهار / يسقط فجأة): a building falls down, a person falls because of weakness, and a plan fails.
✗ become weaker slowly over many years: collapse is sudden, not slow.
✗ stop for a short time and then start again: that is a pause; something that collapses does not just carry on.
✗ be pushed over by someone else: collapse happens because of weakness or failure, not because someone pushes.

questions.prompt: When the old man started to fall, his grandson quickly ___ his arm and held him up.
questions.explanation:
✓ grabbed = took hold of something quickly and strongly (أمسك بسرعة وبقوة) — that is how you stop someone from falling.
✗ grieved: felt very sad because someone died.
✗ grazed: scraped the skin lightly (grazed his knee) — it cannot hold anyone up.
✗ graded: gave a mark or level, as a teacher grades exams.

questions.prompt: "The lifeguard managed to grab the swimmer's hand just before the big wave hit." Which verb is the closest in meaning to "grab"?
questions.explanation:
✓ seize = take hold of something suddenly and firmly (يمسك بقوة) — very close to grab.
✗ release: let go of something — the opposite.
✗ shake: move something up and down; "shake someone's hand" is a greeting, not catching them quickly.
✗ stroke: move your hand gently over something, for example a cat.

questions.prompt: "The sudden beep grabbed the nurse's attention." This means the beep ___.
options: took her phone away from her
questions.explanation:
✓ quickly made her notice it: "grab someone's attention" = make them notice something quickly (لفت انتباهها فورًا). Here "grab" is not about hands.
✗ made her feel pain: a beep is a sound; it does not cause pain.
✗ was ignored by her: the opposite — she noticed it at once.
✗ took her phone away from her: this takes "grab" literally (take something quickly with the hand).

questions.prompt: After a moment's ___, the young doctor agreed to stitch the wound herself.
questions.explanation:
✓ hesitation (noun) = a short pause because you are not sure (تردد). After "a moment's" we need a noun.
✗ hesitant: an adjective (She was hesitant) — it needs a noun after it.
✗ hesitantly: an adverb (She answered hesitantly) — it describes a verb, not "a moment's".
✗ hesitate: the verb (Don't hesitate to ask) — a verb cannot follow "a moment's".

questions.prompt: CPR helps someone whose heart has stopped. It is done by pressing hard and fast on the centre of the person's ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ chest: CPR (الإنعاش القلبي الرئوي) uses chest compressions — pushing down on the centre of the chest again and again — to keep the blood moving.
✗ forehead: part of the face; pressing it does not help the heart.
✗ wrist: where you can feel the pulse, but you do not press on it during CPR.
✗ back: the person lies on their back during CPR; you press on the front of the body, not the back.

questions.prompt: The nurse placed two fingers on the patient's wrist to feel his ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ pulse = the regular beating of the heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck (النبض).
✗ pupil: the black circle in the middle of the eye, or a school student.
✗ purse: a small bag for money.
✗ pause: a short stop in speaking or doing something.

questions.prompt: The doctor ___ the boy's pulse and found that his heart was beating very fast.
questions.explanation:
✓ take someone's pulse = measure how fast their heart is beating (يقيس النبض). You can also say "check someone's pulse".
✗ made: we do not say "make someone's pulse".
✗ did: we do not say "do someone's pulse".
✗ gave: we do not say "give someone's pulse".

questions.prompt: Which is the correct meaning of "pulse"?
options: the force of the blood pushing against the walls of the blood vessels
the regular beating of the heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck
the sound of hospital machines working
the amount of air that your lungs can hold
questions.answer: the regular beating of the heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck
questions.explanation:
✓ the regular beating of the heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck = pulse (النبض).
✗ the force of the blood pushing against the walls of the blood vessels: this is blood pressure (ضغط الدم), a different measurement.
✗ the sound of hospital machines working: this is a buzz (or beeping), not a pulse.
✗ the amount of air that your lungs can hold: this is lung capacity.

questions.prompt: You should start CPR immediately if a person ___.
options: has a very fast pulse after running
is not breathing and has no pulse
has fainted but is breathing normally
is clutching his chest but can still talk
questions.answer: is not breathing and has no pulse
questions.explanation:
✓ is not breathing and has no pulse: CPR (الإنعاش القلبي الرئوي) is for someone whose heart has stopped.
✗ has a very fast pulse after running: a fast pulse after exercise is normal — the heart is working.
✗ has fainted but is breathing normally: the heart is still working, so CPR is not needed — lay the person on their back, raise their legs, and call for help if they do not wake up within a minute.
✗ is clutching his chest but can still talk: he needs an ambulance at once, but his heart is still beating, so CPR is not started.

questions.prompt: The injured man lost ___ and didn't wake up for two hours.
questions.explanation:
✓ consciousness = the state of being awake and aware of what is happening around you (الوعي). "Lose consciousness" = faint, become unconscious.
✗ conscience: the feeling inside you that tells you what is right and wrong (الضمير).
✗ consequence: a result of something.
✗ confidence: belief in yourself (الثقة) — "lost confidence" is correct English, but it does not explain why he didn't wake up.

questions.prompt: The patient was ___ when the paramedics arrived, so they couldn't ask him any questions.
questions.explanation:
✓ unconscious = not awake and not aware of what is happening (فاقد الوعي). That is why he couldn't answer questions.
✗ conscientious: careful to do your work well and correctly.
✗ conscious: awake and aware — then they could ask him questions.
✗ self-conscious: worried about what other people think of you.

questions.prompt: After ten minutes of CPR, the woman finally ___ consciousness.
questions.explanation:
✓ regain consciousness = become awake and aware again (استعاد الوعي) — the opposite of "lose consciousness".
✗ returned: we can say "her consciousness returned", but not "she returned consciousness".
✗ repaired: fixed something that was broken, such as a machine.
✗ remained: stayed in the same state; "remained consciousness" is wrong (we say "remained conscious").

questions.prompt: My legs ached after every training session, but I kept going — "___", as my coach says — and in the end I won the race.
questions.explanation:
✓ No pain, no gain: you must work hard and accept difficulty to succeed (لا نجاح بدون تعب) — the aching legs led to winning the race.
✗ Pale as a ghost: describes a very pale face from fear or illness, not hard work.
✗ It's raining cats and dogs: about very heavy rain — nothing to do with training.
✗ Teamwork makes the dream work: about people working together; this sentence is about one runner's own hard training and pain, not about teamwork.

questions.prompt: Within minutes of the call, the ___ arrived in an ambulance and gave the injured cyclist emergency care.
questions.explanation:
✓ paramedics = medical workers who give emergency care and take people to hospital by ambulance (المسعفون).
✗ surgeons: doctors who do operations in a hospital; they do not usually come in ambulances.
✗ receptionists: people who welcome visitors and answer the phone.
✗ pharmacists: people who prepare and sell medicines in a pharmacy.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT usually part of a paramedic's job?
options: doing CPR on someone who has collapsed
taking patients to hospital by ambulance
doing major operations in a hospital operating theatre
giving emergency care at the scene of an accident
questions.answer: doing major operations in a hospital operating theatre
questions.explanation:
✓ doing major operations in an operating theatre: this is the work of surgeons in hospital, not of paramedics (المسعفون).
✗ doing CPR on someone who has collapsed: paramedics are trained to do this.
✗ taking patients to hospital by ambulance: also part of a paramedic's job.
✗ giving emergency care at the scene: this is a paramedic's main job.

questions.prompt: In Egypt, call 123 for an ambulance only in an ___ — for example, when someone has collapsed or is not breathing.
questions.explanation:
✓ emergency (noun) = a sudden, dangerous situation that needs action at once (حالة طوارئ). We say "in an emergency" — the lesson is called "Emergency Call".
✗ urgent: an adjective; it cannot follow "an" without a noun.
✗ urgency: the need to act quickly — a quality or feeling, not a situation, so "in an urgency" is wrong.
✗ agency: a business that provides a service (a travel agency).

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "When a visitor ___ in the waiting room, a nurse checked his ___ and started CPR."
questions.explanation:
✓ collapsed – pulse: he fell down suddenly (انهار), so the nurse checked his heartbeat (النبض) before starting CPR.
✗ collapsed – scope: a scope is an instrument for looking inside the body; you do not "check someone's scope" before CPR.
✗ swallowed – shift: swallowing is not a reason for CPR, and "checked his shift" (his working period) makes no sense here.
✗ clutched – pulse: "clutch" needs something that is held (clutched his chest / clutched at the chair); "a visitor clutched in the waiting room" is incomplete.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "By the time the ___ arrived, the man had already lost ___."
questions.explanation:
✓ paramedics – consciousness: the emergency workers (المسعفون) arrived after he had become unconscious (فقد الوعي).
✗ paramedics – conscious: "conscious" is an adjective; after "lost" we need the noun "consciousness".
✗ pulses – consciousness: pulses are heartbeats; they do not "arrive".
✗ paramedics – conscience: conscience is your sense of right and wrong; "lose consciousness" is the phrase for fainting.

questions.prompt: The cut on the patient's forehead was deep, so Dr. Maha had to ___ it.
questions.explanation:
✓ stitch = sew the edges of a wound together with a special needle and thread (يخيط الجرح).
✗ snatch: take something quickly and rudely from someone.
✗ stretch: pull something to make it longer or wider — this would make a cut worse.
✗ switch: turn a machine on or off, or change from one thing to another.

questions.prompt: "Dr. Maha prepared to stitch a deep cut." Here, "stitch" means ___.
options: close the cut by sewing its edges together
give an injection to stop the pain
cover the cut with a bandage
questions.answer: close the cut by sewing its edges together
questions.explanation:
✓ close the cut by sewing its edges together: stitching uses a needle and thread to close a deep wound (يخيط).
✗ clean the cut with water: doctors clean a wound before stitching it, but that is not what "stitch" means.
✗ give an injection to stop the pain: this is giving an anaesthetic, not stitching.
✗ cover the cut with a bandage: this is bandaging; it covers a wound but does not close it.

questions.prompt: The cut was so deep that he needed six ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ stitches (noun) = the small pieces of thread that close a wound (غُرز): "He needed six stitches."
✗ scopes: medical instruments for looking inside the body — they do not close cuts.
✗ switches: buttons for turning machines on and off.
✗ pulses: heartbeats.

questions.prompt: The flat part of the face between the eyebrows and the hair is the ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ forehead = the part of the face above the eyes (الجبهة).
✗ chin: the part of the face below the mouth (الذقن).
✗ neck: the part of the body between the head and the shoulders (الرقبة).
✗ cheek: the soft part of the face below each eye (الخد).

questions.prompt: Which is the best description of CPR?
options: a medicine given to someone who has lost consciousness
a test that measures how fast your pulse is
an emergency procedure that uses chest compressions to help someone whose heart has stopped
a machine that beeps when a patient's heart stops
questions.answer: an emergency procedure that uses chest compressions to help someone whose heart has stopped
questions.explanation:
✓ CPR (الإنعاش القلبي الرئوي) is an emergency procedure: you press hard and fast on the chest (chest compressions) to help someone whose heart has stopped.
✗ a medicine: CPR is not medication — nothing is swallowed or injected.
✗ a test that measures your pulse: that is taking someone's pulse.
✗ a machine that beeps: that is a heart monitor; CPR is something people do with their hands, not a machine.

questions.prompt: The football player lay on the grass, ___ with pain and holding his knee.
questions.explanation:
✓ groaning = making a long, deep sound because of pain (يئن).
✗ glowing: shining with a soft light, or looking happy and healthy.
✗ growing: becoming bigger.
✗ grinning: smiling widely — not what you do when you are in pain.

questions.prompt: "A teenager with a broken arm moaned quietly." "Moaned" means he ___.
options: made a long, low sound because he was in pain
questions.answer: made a long, low sound because he was in pain
questions.explanation:
✓ made a long, low sound because he was in pain: to moan (يتأوه / يئن) is to make this sound of pain or unhappiness.
✗ shouted angrily at the nurse: moaning is quiet and low, not loud and angry.
✗ held his arm very tightly: that is "clutch", not "moan".
✗ smiled because he felt better: a teenager with a broken arm who is moaning is not smiling.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "moan" have the same meaning as in "A teenager with a broken arm moaned quietly"?
options: He's always moaning about the hospital food.
She moaned that the bus was late again.
The injured man moaned as they lifted him onto the bed.
Stop moaning and do your homework!
questions.answer: The injured man moaned as they lifted him onto the bed.
questions.explanation:
✓ "The injured man moaned as they lifted him onto the bed." — a long, low sound of pain (يتأوه), as in the story.
✗ "always moaning about the hospital food": here moan = complain again and again (يتذمر) — a different meaning.
✗ "She moaned that the bus was late again": moan that… = complain that… — not a sound of pain.
✗ "Stop moaning and do your homework!": stop complaining — again the meaning "complain".

questions.prompt: The moment the heart monitor beeped, the nurses ___ and started CPR.
questions.explanation:
✓ jumped into action = started doing something at once, quickly and with energy (بدأوا العمل فورًا) — "The moment … beeped" shows how fast they reacted.
✗ were soaked to the skin: completely wet from the rain — nothing to do with the monitor.
✗ kicked back: relaxed — the opposite of starting CPR.
✗ went the extra mile: did more than expected — the sentence is about a fast reaction, not extra effort.

questions.prompt: Pale and frightened, the injured worker ___ his bleeding hand, trying not to cry out.
questions.explanation:
✓ clutched = held tightly, usually because of fear or pain (قبض على / أمسك بإحكام).
✗ clicked: made a short, sharp sound, or pressed a computer mouse.
✗ clattered: made a loud noise of hard things hitting each other.
✗ clapped: hit his hands together, for example to show he liked a performance.

questions.prompt: "The old man clutched his chest and sat down." "Clutched" means he ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ held it tightly (قبض عليه بإحكام): people often clutch a part of the body that hurts.
✗ washed it carefully: nothing to do with clutch.
✗ hit it hard: clutch means holding, not hitting.
✗ hid it under his coat: clutch is about holding tightly, not hiding.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "clutch" have the same meaning as in "He clutched his bleeding hand"?
options: Press the clutch before you change gear.
She carried a small silver clutch to the party.
The bird sat on a clutch of five eggs.
The scared boy clutched the rope as the boat rocked.
questions.answer: The scared boy clutched the rope as the boat rocked.
questions.explanation:
✓ "clutched the rope" = held it tightly because he was afraid (قبض على) — the same meaning as in the story.
✗ "Press the clutch": a pedal in a car.
✗ "a small silver clutch": a clutch bag — a small, flat bag that you carry in your hand, especially at formal events.
✗ "a clutch of five eggs": a group of eggs laid at the same time.

questions.prompt: The toddler had ___ a coin, so the doctors used a flexible scope to take it out.
questions.explanation:
✓ swallowed = made something go down the throat (بلع).
✗ swollen: the past participle of "swell" (become bigger) — "had swollen a coin" is not possible.
✗ followed: went after someone or something.
✗ hollowed: made empty inside.

questions.prompt: In which sentence is "swallow" a verb meaning "make food or drink go down your throat"?
options: One swallow does not make a summer.
A swallow has built a nest under our roof.
We watched the swallows fly south for the winter.
My throat hurts every time I swallow.
questions.answer: My throat hurts every time I swallow.
questions.explanation:
✓ "My throat hurts every time I swallow." — a verb: making food or drink go down the throat (يبلع).
✗ "One swallow does not make a summer": a saying; here "swallow" is a noun — the bird.
✗ "A swallow has built a nest": a noun — a small bird (طائر السنونو).
✗ "the swallows fly south": the bird again, in the plural.

questions.prompt: The child couldn't ___ the big pill, so the nurse crushed it and mixed it with juice.
questions.explanation:
✓ swallow = make something go down the throat (يبلع). A big pill can be hard to swallow.
✗ sway: move slowly from side to side.
✗ sweep: clean a floor with a brush.
✗ swell: become bigger, like a swollen ankle.

questions.prompt: Using a long, flexible ___ with a tiny camera, the doctor looked inside the patient's stomach.
questions.explanation:
✓ scope = a medical instrument with a long, thin tube (often with a camera) used to look inside the body (منظار طبي).
✗ scoop: a tool like a large, deep spoon, used for picking up flour or serving ice cream — it has no camera for looking inside the stomach.
✗ scale: a machine for weighing things.
✗ slope: a surface that goes up or down, like the side of a hill.

questions.prompt: "Using a flexible scope, the doctors carefully removed the coin." Here, "scope" means ___.
options: a strong medicine that stops pain
a small, sharp knife used in operations
a medical instrument used to see inside the body
the range of things that a subject deals with
questions.answer: a medical instrument used to see inside the body
questions.explanation:
✓ a medical instrument used to see inside the body (منظار): with it, the doctors could see the coin and remove it.
✗ a strong medicine that stops pain: this is a painkiller.
✗ a small, sharp knife used in operations: this is a scalpel.
✗ the range of things that a subject deals with: "scope" has this meaning too (the scope of a project), but not in this sentence — you cannot remove a coin "using a range".

questions.prompt: The patient needs ___ treatment; he could die if we wait any longer.
questions.explanation:
✓ urgent (adjective) = needing to be dealt with immediately (عاجل). An adjective is needed before the noun "treatment".
✗ urge: a verb (urge someone to do something) or a noun (a strong wish) — "urge treatment" is wrong here.
✗ urgency: a noun (the need to act quickly) — "urgency treatment" is wrong.
✗ urgently: an adverb (He needs treatment urgently) — it cannot come before a noun.

questions.prompt: There is always a real sense of ___ in the emergency room at night.
questions.explanation:
✓ a sense of urgency = the feeling that things must be done quickly (إحساس بضرورة الإسراع). After "a sense of" we need a noun.
✗ urgently: an adverb — it cannot follow "a sense of".
✗ chaotic: an adjective (we would need the noun "chaos").
✗ urgent: an adjective — "a sense of urgent" is wrong.

questions.prompt: "The night in the emergency room was full of fear and urgency." Here, "urgency" means ___.
options: a feeling of calm and peace
the need to deal with something quickly
questions.answer: the need to deal with something quickly
questions.explanation:
✓ the need to deal with something quickly (ضرورة الإسراع / الإلحاح): in an emergency room, lives depend on fast action.
✗ a lack of interest: this is indifference.
✗ a long period of waiting: urgency is about acting fast, not waiting.
✗ a feeling of calm and peace: the opposite of a night full of fear and urgency.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "There was ___ all around the crash site, but the young paramedic worked calmly with a sense of ___."
questions.explanation:
✓ chaos – urgency: "but" contrasts the disorder at the crash site (فوضى) with the paramedic's calm, fast work (إحساس بضرورة الإسراع).
✗ order – urgency: if everything was in order, "but … calmly" would not be a contrast.
✗ chaos – pulse: a pulse is a heartbeat; "a sense of pulse" makes no sense.
✗ chaotic – urgent: both are adjectives; we need nouns after "There was" and "a sense of".

questions.prompt: He bit his lip, trying not to ___ in pain as the nurse cleaned the wound.
questions.explanation:
✓ cry out = shout or make a loud sound suddenly because of pain or fear (يصرخ).
✗ cry off: (British, informal) say that you cannot do something you promised to do.
✗ call off: cancel an event (call off the match).
✗ carry out: do a task (carry out an operation).

questions.prompt: "The worker clutched his bleeding hand, trying not to cry out." "Cry out" means ___.
options: complain about something again and again
shout suddenly because of pain or fear
questions.answer: shout suddenly because of pain or fear
questions.explanation:
✓ shout suddenly because of pain or fear (يصرخ): cry out = make a sudden loud sound.
✗ weep quietly with tears: this is a meaning of "cry" on its own; "cry out" is about a loud sound, not tears.
✗ complain about something again and again: this is "moan about".
✗ phone someone for help: that is "call for help".

questions.prompt: "Outside, it was raining cats and dogs." This means ___.
options: the weather was cold but dry
animals were running in the rain
questions.explanation:
✓ it was raining very heavily (تمطر بغزارة): "rain cats and dogs" is an idiom; it has nothing to do with animals.
✗ the weather was cold but dry: it was raining, so it was not dry.
✗ it was raining a little: that is drizzle — the opposite of heavy rain.
✗ animals were running in the rain: this takes the idiom literally.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the idiom correctly?
options: There's only a light drizzle; it's raining cats and dogs.
After the operation, the patient was raining cats and dogs.
It's raining cats and dogs, so let's sit in the garden and enjoy the sun.
Take an umbrella — it's raining cats and dogs out there.
questions.answer: Take an umbrella — it's raining cats and dogs out there.
questions.explanation:
✓ "Take an umbrella — it's raining cats and dogs out there." — the idiom means raining very heavily (تمطر بغزارة), so an umbrella makes sense.
✗ "There's only a light drizzle; it's raining cats and dogs": a light drizzle is very light rain — the opposite of the idiom.
✗ "the patient was raining cats and dogs": the idiom describes the weather, not a person.
✗ "…so let's sit in the garden and enjoy the sun": heavy rain and sitting in the sun do not go together.

questions.prompt: Dr. Basem had left his umbrella at home, so in the heavy rain he arrived at the hospital ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ soaked to the skin = completely wet, from head to toe (مبلل تمامًا) — what happens in heavy rain without an umbrella.
✗ as pale as a ghost: very pale because of fear, shock or illness — leaving an umbrella at home does not cause this.
✗ as dry as a bone: completely dry — the opposite.
✗ on a rollercoaster: a ride, or a situation with ups and downs; it has nothing to do with rain.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "Outside, it was ___, and Dr. Basem ran into the hospital ___."
options: raining cats and dogs – going the extra mile
raining cats and dogs – soaked to the skin
springing into action – soaked to the skin
soaked to the skin – raining cats and dogs
questions.answer: raining cats and dogs – soaked to the skin
questions.explanation:
✓ raining cats and dogs – soaked to the skin: it was raining very heavily, so he was completely wet (تمطر بغزارة – مبلل تمامًا).
✗ raining cats and dogs – going the extra mile: "going the extra mile" means making extra effort; it does not describe how he looked after the rain.
✗ springing into action – soaked to the skin: "it was springing into action" makes no sense for the weather.
✗ soaked to the skin – raining cats and dogs: the weather cannot be "soaked to the skin", and a person cannot be "raining cats and dogs".

questions.prompt: When she saw the X-ray of her son's broken leg, her face went as pale as a ___.
questions.explanation:
✓ as pale as a ghost = extremely pale, usually because of fear, shock or illness (شاحب جدًا).
✗ tomato: a tomato is red, so this comparison would describe a red face (for example from embarrassment), not a pale one.
✗ beetroot: we say "as red as a beetroot" (British English) — a red face, for example from anger or embarrassment, not a pale one.
✗ rose: roses are usually red or pink; we do not use them to mean pale.

questions.prompt: Mr. Ramy made a quick ___ after his surgery and went home after a week.
questions.explanation:
✓ recovery (noun) = the process of getting well again (التعافي / الشفاء). "make a quick recovery" is a common phrase.
✗ recover: the verb (He recovered quickly) — a verb cannot follow "a quick".
✗ recovered: the past form of the verb — not a noun.
✗ discovery: finding something for the first time — it sounds similar but has a different meaning.

questions.prompt: "Without hesitation, the team jumped into action." This means the team acted ___.
options: immediately, without pausing because they were unsure
questions.answer: immediately, without pausing because they were unsure
questions.explanation:
✓ immediately, without pausing because they were unsure: hesitation (تردد) is a pause before you do something because you are not sure; "without hesitation" = at once.
✗ only after the doctor arrived: this would mean they waited — the sentence says they acted at once.
✗ slowly and very carefully: the opposite of acting without hesitation.
✗ unwillingly, after a long argument: acting unwillingly is the opposite of acting without hesitation.

questions.prompt: Mr. Ramy has been ___ from heart surgery for a few days, and he is getting stronger every day.
questions.explanation:
✓ recover from = get well again after an illness or an operation (يتعافى / يتماثل للشفاء).
✗ uncovering: removing a cover, or finding out a secret.
✗ covering: putting something over something else.
✗ discovering: finding something for the first time.

questions.prompt: Choose the pair that completes the sentence: "The nurse ___ the medication, but the little boy refused to ___ it."
questions.explanation:
✓ administered – swallow: the nurse gave the medicine (أعطت الدواء), but the boy would not let it go down his throat (يبلع).
✗ groaned – swallow: "groan" (make a sound of pain) does not take an object such as "the medication".
✗ admitted – swallow: "admit" means accept someone into hospital or agree that something is true; you do not admit a medicine.
✗ administered – stitch: you stitch a cut, not a medicine.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes CHAOS, not just a BUZZ?
options: People were running and shouting in every direction, and nobody knew what to do.
The café was full of the happy sound of people chatting.
There was excitement in the class before the school trip.
The machines in the factory were humming steadily.
questions.answer: People were running and shouting in every direction, and nobody knew what to do.
questions.explanation:
✓ People running and shouting in every direction, with nobody knowing what to do = complete confusion and disorder (فوضى).
✗ the happy sound of people chatting: this is a buzz of conversation — busy and noisy, but not disorder.
✗ excitement in the class before the trip: a buzz of excitement — lively, but not complete disorder.
✗ machines humming steadily: the buzz of machines working — organised, not chaotic.
